hyps.why: At already-large learning rates, further increases cause divergence and dead ReLUs, so the edit hurts much more than elsewhere.
At tiny learning rates the network is undertrained after 243 epochs, so raising the rate yields large gains.
Lowering an unstable learning rate rescues training, giving much larger benefit than lowering a moderate one.
With a tiny learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and worsen undertraining.
With a large learning rate, bigger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training.
Raising an already-large L2 penalty causes strong underfitting, whereas increases at small alpha are negligible.
Deeper ReLU nets are more prone to instability and dying units at high learning rates.
Adding units to very narrow networks relieves a capacity bottleneck, while wide networks are already saturated.
Large batches give few updates per epoch, so a higher learning rate compensates for the reduced step count.
Tiny batches combined with a large learning rate amplify gradient noise and cause divergence.
